methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $17M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Hertha Metals is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $17M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 9 private companies and 1 public company (277810.KQ) operating in the robotics and manufacturing sector, including later-stage peers such as Generalist AI ($2.0B, Series B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B, Series B), and Walden Robotics ($1.1B, Seed), alongside earlier private participants including Divergent, Exotec, and Locus Robotics.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using the $17M raised as a proxy for current value and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement, implies a valuation of $34M. Peer-median analysis across the four comparable companies yields a median valuation of $1.7B, with a range spanning $1.1B to $2.0B. The wide dispersion reflects meaningful stage heterogeneity within the peer set: three comparables are Series B stage while one is Seed.

Triangulating these methods produces a valuation range of $29M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $867M. The stage-progression method supplies a floor near $34M, while peer comparables establish an upper boundary near $1.7B–$2.0B. Key uncertainties include the appropriateness of the 2.0x multiplier given Hertha's specific capital efficiency and market dynamics, and whether the peer set adequately reflects differences in technology maturity and addressable market within robotics and manufacturing.
